column1: # comment: Email alignments. EmailMessage is equivalent to schema:EmailMessage; the rest use skos:closeMatch (cross-type/loose) to schema.org, the Nepomuk Message Ontology (NMO), and SIOC. The reified MessageParticipant relator (issue #159) is canonical; flat from/to/cc/bcc and their schema.org/NMO counterparts are lossy projection shortcuts. Trust terms (RelayHop/AuthenticationResult/signatures) are canonical — no maintained external RDF vocabulary exists for them. MessageParticipantRole envelope/resent roles are also canonical — no external vocabulary covers them. threadSubject and subjectPrefix (issue #138) are canonical — no maintained external vocabulary exposes thread-level normalized subject or per-message prefix stripping. MessageKind and its individuals (issue #137) are canonical — no maintained external vocabulary covers DSN/ARF/MDN/auto-generated report kinds. priority, importance, precedence, autoSubmitted, readReceiptRequested, and dispositionNotificationTo (issue #137) are canonical — no maintained external vocabulary covers these behavioral header facets. MIME body-part metadata terms (MultipartBodyPart, InlinePart, MultipartType, ContentDisposition, ContentTransferEncoding, hasMultipartType, hasInlinePart, hasContentDisposition, hasContentTransferEncoding, partId, contentId, charset; issue #133) are canonical — no maintained external RDF vocabulary covers granular MIME structure, Content-ID, transfer encoding, or disposition values. Mailbox hierarchy terms (parentMailbox, childMailbox, mailboxSortOrder, mailboxPath, mailboxTotalMessages, mailboxUnreadMessages; issue #132) are canonical — JMAP (RFC 8621) has no maintained RDF vocabulary. parentMailbox/childMailbox specialize the universal partOf/hasPart spine; path and counts are derived projection state (Principle 12). Calendar invitation bridge terms (describesEvent, calendarAttachment, calendarUid, CalendarMethod, hasCalendarMethod, messageKindCalendarInvitation; issue #139) are canonical — no maintained external RDF vocabulary covers the email→event bridge. iCalendar METHOD/UID alignments are by reference to icaltzd.
